//: Each entry breaks one property the tests claim to protect. A mutation the suite does not catch is an unguarded property, not a curiosity.
//defensive: Marked defensive means the change is expected to survive: the property is held by another guard, or is unreachable through the public API. Recorded rather than deleted, because deleting it would lose the reason.
//filter: A filter of * means the whole suite: the honest filter when the question is whether any test at all covers the code.

mutations.//: Expected to survive. Mix clamps the amount to 0..1 first, so this clamp is never the gate that holds. The two clamps together are the property; see the combined mutation.

mutations.name: colour amount clamp widened
mutations.//: Expected to survive, for the same reason in reverse: the blend still clamps to 0..255, so a wide amount cannot wrap.

mutations.name: colour clamps removed together (the actual guard)
mutations.//: With neither clamp an amount above one over-blends and the byte cast wraps, so the suite must notice.

mutations.name: cache trusts an entry that carries no hash
mutations.//: Once marked defensive, and that label was wrong. This harness used to build and run only the Core suite, so it could not see the Windows suite covering this too. Removing the flag is the honest fix: the property is guarded, by a test in the other suite. A defensive label is only as trustworthy as the harness's scope.

mutations.name: the hash comparison accepts a blank expected hash
mutations.//: Expected to survive for the same reason in the other direction: the fast path returns before this line whenever the expected hash is blank.

mutations.name: cache accepts a blank hash in both places (the actual guard)
mutations.//: With neither guard an entry whose key declares no usable hash is served straight off the disk. The suite must notice.

mutations.new: internal static bool IsMsiexecSuccess(int code) => code is 0 or 3010;
mutations.//: This is the bug the audit found: the table described 1641 as a completed install while the caller filed it under InstallerFailed.

mutations.name: a leaf module reaches sideways into another leaf
mutations.//: A sideways reference, not an upward one. Pointing Core at a layer above it cannot build at all: every layer above Core references Core, so the reference is a cycle and the compiler refuses it. The invariant 'Core references nothing' is therefore held by the build as well as by this test. An acyclic violation - one leaf referencing another - is possible, which is why the probe uses that.

mutations.name: one platform registers four providers and the other five
mutations.//: The providers ship as extension packages now, so the packages a platform assembles are what says which platforms it gets. Both the reference and the copied package are dropped: the invariant reads the package names, so removing only one of the two would leave the count unchanged and prove nothing.

mutations.name: Basic silently becomes the same as Silent
a TODO reappears in the source
the resume bug returns: a whole body is appended to a partial file
mutations.//: This is the bug the decision exists to prevent: the server ignored the range header, so the body starts at zero, and appending it produces a file with its beginning written twice.

mutations.name: elevation is demanded for every package, not just MSIs
an install is called done on the installer's word alone
mutations.//: The fake success the specification forbids: the installer said it worked, and nothing checked. Every install would report success regardless of what the machine actually looks like.

mutations.name: a declared detector is no longer consulted
mutations.//: With this, every entry falls through to the path and record checks, so a detector that says NotDetected is never heard.

mutations.name: the extension context can no longer be unloaded
mutations.//: An extension that cannot be unloaded keeps its files locked, so it cannot be updated or removed without restarting the app.

mutations.name: a missing extension assembly is reported as loaded
mutations.old: return new ExtensionStatus(manifest, ExtensionLoadState.AssemblyMissing, $"Assembly not found: {assemblyPath}");
mutations.new: return new ExtensionStatus(manifest, ExtensionLoadState.Loaded, $"Assembly not found: {assemblyPath}");

mutations.name: the PnP class filter stops filtering
mutations.//: Guarded by the smoke suite, not a unit test: the registry this reads is the real one. The smoke check now asserts discriminating power, so a filter that matches everything fails it. This entry is also the proof that the smoke layer is mutation-covered at all.

mutations.name: an unsigned package is allowed to claim the official trust level
mutations.//: The trust ceiling of a package nobody signed. Raising it lets an unsigned package present itself as official, which is the one thing the signature layer exists to prevent.

mutations.name: the engine selector stops selecting
mutations.//: A selector that never selects is still 'no engine can handle this route' with extra steps, and the aria2 smoke check asserts a specific engine is chosen.

mutations.name: a modified signed binary is reported as valid
mutations.old:
const string text = "安装包的签名与文件内容不匹配，签名后已被修改。";
            return new AuthenticodeResult(AuthenticodeTrust.InvalidSignature, text, signer, issuer);
mutations.new:
const string text = "安装包的签名与文件内容不匹配，签名后已被修改。";
            return new AuthenticodeResult(AuthenticodeTrust.Valid, text, signer, issuer);
mutations.//: The digest mismatch is the whole point of verifying a binary: code that reports the modification and then calls the file Valid has said the right thing and done the wrong one.

mutations.name: a tampered catalog still grants official authority
mutations.//: Only a verified signature confers official authority. Making tampering produce Verified would let edited catalog data drive unattended installs.

mutations.name: the MSIX detector never matches a package
mutations.old:
var matches = regex.IsMatch(package.Name)
                || (package.DisplayName is not null && regex.IsMatch(package.DisplayName));
mutations.//: A detector that never detects reports every installed Store app as missing, which is the difference between Unknown and Missing that the whole product is built around.

mutations.name: the detection suggester proposes nothing
mutations.new:
if (true) { return Array.Empty<DetectionSuggestion>(); }
        var pool = installed
mutations.//: The suggester is how an entry with no detector becomes decidable. Returning nothing leaves the catalog permanently undecided and reports no reason.

mutations.name: a source that needs a sign-in is reported as ready
mutations.//: A share that cannot be fetched without a sign-in must not look like one that can. Calling it Ready hands the installer a source it cannot use and tells the person nothing.

mutations.name: the automatic choice stops being a choice and takes the first listed source
mutations.//: This is the bug that actually shipped: choosing Sources.FirstOrDefault() is declaration order wearing a decision's clothes.

mutations.name: picking stops caring whether the download can be checked
mutations.//: Between two sources that both work, the one whose bytes can be checked afterwards is the one to install.

mutations.name: picking starts depending on which platform it is
mutations.//: Sorting by the platform name makes the winner a platform rather than a source. All five are peers (30/31), so the name must never enter the comparison.

mutations.name: picking prefers a shakier way of obtaining the file
mutations.//: Parsing a web page is what a platform does when it has no interface to call. Preferring it over an official API chooses the method that breaks first.

mutations.name: a share source with no link is reported as usable
mutations.old:
SourceReadiness.Incomplete,
                "这条来源没有写分享链接。",
mutations.new:
SourceReadiness.Ready,
                "这条来源没有写分享链接。",
mutations.//: A share source is identified by its link. Without one there is nothing to fetch, and saying otherwise sends the installer after an empty address.

mutations.name: reading a share stops using the platform the source names
mutations.//: The platform is carried by the source. Falling back to whichever platform is listed first is the same guess by convenience that a domain-name lookup used to be.

mutations.name: an id-only locator is ignored again
mutations.//: An item named by the platform's own id has no folders to walk, so requiring a walk drops the id and falls back to a file-name match that may find nothing or the wrong item.

mutations.name: a download that could not be resolved is reported as done
mutations.//: A resolver that failed has to fail the job. Returning quietly completes it, and the task list then shows success for a download that never happened.

mutations.name: the skin that was switched on is forgotten
mutations.old: var updated = Current with { SkinId = skinId };
mutations.//: Persisting the chosen skin is what makes 启用 mean anything across a restart; without it the platform default comes back.

mutations.name: the override layer stops re-reading the file
mutations.//: Without the clear the layer keeps what it read at startup, so an override written through another instance — including a deletion — never shows up in the live skin list.

mutations.name: picking a share item stops writing the location
mutations.//: The whole point of picking from the share tree is that the path is generated for the author. Clearing it turns the click into a no-op that still reports success.

mutations.name: one save button stops writing colours
mutations.//: The single 保存 has to write both halves. Dropping the colours leaves the user's colour edits on screen but not on disk, and reports success.

mutations.name: a blank text row is written as an edit
mutations.//: A blank row means 'keep the base's wording'. Treating it as an edit makes 保存 report writes that never happened and rewrite the file for nothing.

mutations.name: the navigation rail stops carrying its word key
mutations.//: Without the key the editor cannot offer the rail entry's own word for editing: the preview's sidebar items become unselectable-as-text.
